claims.text: The starting material is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi alloy powder.
The proposed intervention is laser powder bed fusion with the build platform maintained at approximately 300–400 °C.
The comparison is against room-temperature-platform LPBF with otherwise similar laser power, scan strategy, and atmosphere.
Platform preheating reduces the temperature difference between the melt pool and the substrate.
Reducing the melt-pool-to-substrate temperature difference decreases thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower thermal gradients attenuate rapid cooling rates.
Rapid cooling can cause localized compositional segregation in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
High thermal gradients and rapid cooling promote residual-stress formation in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Platform preheating reduces compositional segregation relative to room-temperature-platform LPBF.
Platform preheating lowers residual stress relative to room-temperature-platform LPBF.
Platform preheating decreases defect density relative to room-temperature-platform LPBF.
Reduced residual stress, segregation, and defect density improve the mechanical integrity of as-built AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated-platform builds are expected to have greater strength than room-temperature-platform builds.
Preheated-platform builds are expected to have greater ductility than room-temperature-platform builds.
Room-temperature-platform LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces significant thermal gradients, segregation, residual-stress buildup, and defects.
The proposed effect is scoped to LPBF at the specified preheating range and is not claimed to transfer directly to casting, deposition, or other preheating temperatures.
